Subject: PaymentsCo — API auth & key management (post-call recap)

Hi Sophie / Carlos,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery focused on API authentication and key management for the PaymentsCo integration: 

Recap:
- Primary integration modes you mentioned: server-to-server backend calls for payment enrichment + a lightweight client-side widget for contextual assistance.
- Security & compliance drivers: short-lived credentials, audit logs, and automated key rotation.
- Architecture constraints: no public keys embedded in client; prefer service-account style provisioning for backend microservices.

Technical notes / recommended approach (high level):
- Service accounts + short-lived JWTs (recommended): Redwood supports issuing and verifying short-lived tokens (JWTs) via a client-credentials/OIDC flow and can accept tokens signed by your KMS-backed signing keys (we also support our managed token minting for Private/Dedicated customers). This avoids long-lived secrets in environment variables.
- OAuth 2.0 client credentials: a good compromise if you already have an OAuth stack; Redwood accepts bearer tokens and verifies via JWKS.
- API keys: supported for quick PoC; rotate via the API-key rotation endpoints every 30 days and use per-service keys (i.e., one key per service). For hosted deployments we provide key rotation endpoints and token-scoped keys; for Dedicated/Private we recommend KMS/HSM integration for auto-rotation.
- Key rotation: recommend automated rotation with grace period + audit logging. We can integrate with your KMS (AWS KMS/Google KMS) for private deployments.
- SDK setup & env vars: we have SDKs (Node/Python/Go) that accept either API_KEY or a short-lived TOKEN. We'll share code samples.
- Routing & structured outputs: if you plan to use tool calling / structured outputs, we recommend pinning model-version + model-variant for deterministic outputs; auth is orthogonal but ensure any tool endpoints validate the same tokens.
- Embeddings / rerankers: treat embedding keys separately and use scoped keys or service accounts that only have embedding inference permission. This reduces blast radius.

Attachments shared after the call: Redwood_Auth_Key_Management_Guide.pdf (high-level), integration_snippet_samples.zip (SDK snippets).

Next steps / asks: 
1) We'll send the security questionnaire back filled (you mentioned SOC 2 artifacts) — see attached.
2) Tech deep-dive with Alex (solutions engineering) to walk through JWT minting and a short demo of the SDK. Can you share 60–90 minute slots next week?
3) Please confirm whether you prefer managed token minting from Redwood or if you'll provision service accounts in your IAM (we can support both).
4) If you have an allowlist for egress IPs, please send that over; otherwise we'll provide our published ranges for Hosted/Dedicated.

Happy to sync — I’ll propose slots in a follow-up.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Hi Sophie — thanks for the questions, inline answers below. I've attached our filled questionnaire and the short guide with example env vars/snippets.

> 1) Token lifetime / renewal / revocation
- Recommended lifetime: 5–15 minutes for short-lived access tokens for high-security flows; 1 hour is common for lower-risk background jobs. For PoC we recommend 15 minutes.
- Renewal cadence: client should request a new token just before expiry; typical flow is client hits your auth service (or Redwood managed mint endpoint) to exchange a long-lived service credential for a short-lived token.
- Revocation: for JWTs we recommend key rotation at the signing-key level and a short token TTL; Redwood also supports a token revocation list for sessions issued by Redwood-managed minting. For API keys we support immediate revocation via the admin API.

> 2) JWKS support
- Yes — Redwood accepts JWTs and verifies them against your JWKS endpoint (we cache keys and respect cache-control headers). We also publish our JWKS for customers who want to verify our tokens.

> 3) API key auto-rotation on Hosted
- Hosted: we provide API endpoints to create/rotate/revoke keys. Rotation can be scripted via our admin API; "automatic" rotation (i.e., zero-touch rolling replacement) is available for Dedicated/Private when integrated with your KMS — for Hosted we can run scheduled rotations but you'll need to consume the new key (we can provide a webhook that notifies your CI to pull new keys).

> 4) Example env vars & SDK snippet (Node) — see integration_snippet_samples.zip for full samples. Tiny inline example below:

Node (pseudo):
const Redwood = require('@redwood-ai/sdk');
// API key usage
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
// Short-lived token usage
const clientToken = new Redwood({ token: process.env.REDWOOD_SHORT_LIVED_TOKEN });

// token minting flow (very high level)
// your service -> your auth (service account) -> exchange for short-lived token -> call Redwood API with Bearer token

> 5) SOC 2 + questionnaire
